transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-07
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood CSM), Anika Rao (BlueMercury lead ML), Jon Park (BlueMercury Infra), Sophie Grant (BlueMercury Product), Marco Li (BlueMercury SRE)

Summary: quick retrofit review of the hybrid kernel sampling experiments from last week, some odd microburst p99s, discussion on TTFT vs streaming buffer tradeoffs, sequence length distribution sanity check, and next steps to capture traces and schedule kernel deep-dive.

Topics: hybrid kernels, TTFT (first token fast time), streaming handshake/queueing, seqlen distribution, KV cache hits, packet microbursts, encryption/KMS constraints, SOC2 request

[00:00] Maya (AE): ok hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: recap the hybrid kernel sample runs, show the anomalies we saw and decide next steps.
[00:18] Anika: hey thanks, excited. we got your run results, saw a couple of spikes, want to understand if this is runtime or our traffic shape.
[00:30] Liam (SE): yeah so to frame it, last week we flipped the sampling to try mixing the f32-ish kernel for seqlen > 1k and the quantized kernel for short sequences, hope was to keep TTFT low while saving cost on 90% of short calls.
[01:05] Jon (Infra): small note, our traffic is chatty — many short messages but with occasional long system prompts that push seq to 1.5k. we might be the oddball.
[01:28] Liam: got it, that explains the p99 microbursts. when the scheduler moves from the fast quantized path to the heavier kernel there's a wake-up cost and KV cache reconciling, we saw a 180-280ms jump in a subset.
[01:50] Sophie: by "wake-up" do you mean cold start on kernel or GPU memory thrash?
[02:08] Liam: a bit of both, the runtime does kernel switchover and sometimes rebinds the attention kernels, that can bump TTFB. also we saw some cross-talk with our batching window causing extra queueing.
[02:38] Anika: hmm, our SLO is 250ms TTFT p95 and 400ms p99. those 280+ cases are pushing us.
[02:50] Maya: right; couple of options: keep a single fast path tuned for our median seqlen, or do the hybrid but add hedging/early-response path to catch the switchers.
[03:10] Marco (SRE): curious about streaming. some of our flows use streaming to present partial tokens — does switching kernels mess up streaming handshake? we saw truncated streams once.
[03:31] Liam: yes, streaming adds complexity. if kernel switch happens mid-stream we have to flush KV's and convert state, that can cause a small pause and sometimes the stream client sees an incomplete chunk.
[03:55] Jon: that matches our logs, one call had a 120ms gap in stream. not catastrophic but visible to users.
[04:12] Priya (CSM): quick callout — we captured the run artifacts in the shared folder: https://redwood.app/poc/blue-mercury/latency-run-20260106.csv and a short mp4 of the streaming gap.
[04:35] Anika: perfect. we also attached our seqlen histogram which shows a bimodal distribution — lots under 200, a small tail around 1-2k from system prompts.
[04:52] Liam: that bimodal is exactly the cause. hybrid helps cost but needs smart hedging: either pre-classify requests that will go long or keep lightweight early-response that returns first tokens from the quantized kernel while the heavy kernel warms.
[05:12] Sophie: does Redwood support early-response multiplexing?
[05:20] Liam: yes, we have an "early-response" policy in runtime but it needs config: how long to wait for heavy kernel, whether to merge sequences, etc. currently it's experimental for hybrid quantized->full kernels.
[05:45] Maya: agenda item: decide whether we pursue hedging now or fall back to single path for the PoC. thoughts?
[06:00] Anika: lean hedging but we need guarantees — we can't ship user-visible truncations.
[06:12] Liam: totally, proposal: run 2 experiments this week — A) hedging with 50ms early-response timeout, keep streaming enabled, B) single unified kernel tuned for median seqlen and disable hybrid. collect p95/p99 TTFT and streaming gap metrics.
[06:35] Marco: do you have an estimate on cost delta? hedging seems like more GPU work.
[06:42] Maya: we'll model both — hedging will increase token-cost by approx 5-12% but may cut p99 by ~30-60% depending on mix. we'll share a banded TCO.
[06:58] Jon: also want to ensure KMS/encryption doesn't slow kernel transitions. our environment forces HSM sign calls on certain paths.
[07:12] Liam: good flag — if your key ops are in the hot-path we need to isolate them or cache auth tokens longer. Anika, can you confirm which calls require HSM?
[07:24] Anika: yes I'll confirm — some of the system prompts are labeled PCI and go through extra signing.
[07:33] Liam: ok that might explain extra tail latency on those sequences.
[07:45] [08:00] Quick playback and look at the CSV (screen-share notes)
[08:00] Liam: looking at run id 20260106-run3, this spike at 14:34 shows kernel swap at token 12 and then a 230ms extra wall time. the KV cache hit rate dropped to 48% for that request.
[08:30] Anika: KV cash? I mean KV cache, sorry transcription. but 48% seems odd. we thought cache should be over 80% given our prefix reuse.
[08:48] Liam: the prefix diverged because of injected system prompts; those are unique so cache miss is expected. we can pre-warm some prefixes but need to be careful with user data.
[09:10] Sophie: any privacy concerns with pre-warming? we can't store sensitive prompts in cache.
[09:22] Liam: agreed. pre-warm could be synthetic or general system prompts, not user content. or use encrypted transient cache that evicts immediately.
[09:38] Marco: can we test a config where system prompts are pinned to a local warm cache so they don't cause swaps?
[09:48] Liam: yes, we can run a pinned-prefix experiment. that'll be one of the test runs.
[10:02] [10:15] Discussion of measurement windows and sampling frequency
[10:15] Maya: small ask from product side: put the SLO banding on the dashboard so we can see p50/p95/p99 color bands.
[10:25] Priya: we can add that for the PoC dashboard, will need a quick permissions bump for BlueMercury team.
[10:35] Anika: also we want lookback on the streaming gaps tied to client-side metrics — we'll share client logs.
[10:45] Jon: on infra, we noticed a couple of container restarts during overnight runs. not sure if it's OOM or runtime asserts.
[10:55] Liam: there were some OOMs in the larger kernel under certain batch sizes; we need to cap batch concurrency for the heavy kernel or allocate a bit more GPU mem.
[11:10] Sophie: are you suggesting we tune batching windows by kernel type?
[11:18] Liam: yes. runtime supports per-kernel batching windows; for the heavy kernel we can reduce the max-batch and prefer more frequent small dispatches to avoid OOM and reduce latency tails, but that increases cost.
[11:38] Anika: what's the recommended sequence length threshold for switching? we tried 1024 last week.
[11:45] Liam: from the sample set, threshold 800-900 would've caught most longs earlier but we'd still misclassify ~6% — tradeoff between cost and misses. we'll iterate.
[12:00] Marco: can we instrument pre-classifier at client side so you only send to heavy kernel when sequence will exceed threshold?
[12:09] Liam: yes, local pre-classifier is low-cost and recommended for production; for PoC we can do a soft classifier at the edge to route early.
[12:24] Anika: ok we can prototype that quickly.
[12:35] [12:50] Quick Q&A on compliance
[12:50] Sophie: on SOC2 and audit logs, do you provide immutable audit logs per request and can we push logs to our S3?
[13:00] Maya: yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated can ship audit logs to customer S3 or Kafka; for hosted we have a redacted audit export. will send the SOC2 pack.
[13:12] Anika: please include retention and encryption details, and the SOC2 point of contact.
[13:20] Maya: will do.
[13:28] [13:40] Recap and explicit next steps
[13:40] Maya: recap: we'll run two experiments (hedge vs single-path), Liam will capture microburst traces and kernel utilization, BlueMercury will provide prompt set and confirm KMS/HSM gating, Maya will share TCO and SOC2 docs. schedule kernel deep-dive weds.
[13:58] Sophie: sounds good. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References: https://redwood.app/poc/blue-mercury/latency-run-20260106.csv, https://redwood.app/poc/blue-mercury/stream-gap-clip-20260106.mp4

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-words (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache), speaker labels may be approximate.
